hitl_conditions: Not discussed as such; the framework aims to minimise human effort in picking and replenishment while workers remain the executors in manual picker-to-parts hubs; deployment in robotic parts-to-picker warehouses is left to future research.
key_finding: A DT/IoT-based framework for Physical Internet city hubs embeds ANFIS demand forecasting and a joint order-fulfilment/replenishment optimisation model; simulation of a 600-SKU forward-reserve hub shows joint, forecast-driven operations cut daily picker travel by 80.9% and reserve-area visits by 79.8% versus standalone operations.
citation_locator: Key finding: Sec. 5.2.1-5.2.2 (Tables 3-4) and Sec. 6. Twin/AI design: Sec. 4 (4.1-4.3.3), Appendix A. HITL evidence: Sec. 3 (decision-support definition), 4.1 (worker data capture), 4.2 (direct CS-to-PS feedback, worker task notifications), 5.2.1 (manpower savings), 7 (minimise human effort). HTML version, no page numbers.

quotes.text: DTs in the CS are the virtual representations of the physical entities such as PI containers. They abstract the features of a physical entity based on the heterogeneous IoT data streamed from the PS and PI-orders from WMS.
the physical environment is a PI-hub with a storage area subdivided into a forward area and a reserve area [...] workers can indicate the start and end of each of their assigned tasks via the devices

machine learning-based models are constructed for three tasks: (i) order synchronization mechanism using a proactive lookahead scheme, (ii) order arrival prediction using an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system and (iii) optimization of joint OFR based on predicted order arrival

the TIS strategy is defined as the integration of cyber-physical systems and internet of things for digitally visualizing and sharing all relevant internal information and decisions among stakeholders in a warehouse with operational decision support enabled by machine learning-based optimizations

an important feature of the cyber-to-physical communication is to allow direct feedback fed from the CS to the PS [...] workers can receive notifications from their handheld devices about new order picking tasks assigned to them

Human still plays a leading role in the management and execution of both the inbound and outbound order fulfillment process in the coming decade [...] in order to minimize human efforts in the OFR while maintaining an adequate level of throughput

ft_note: Incluido: gemelo digital+IoT diseñado como arquitectura (espacio físico/ciberespacio, flujos de datos) para un hub PI urbano; IA = ANFIS neuro-difuso que prevé llegadas de pedidos, acoplado a un MIP de picking/reposición conjunta; el gemelo no se implementa, solo se simula el modelo OFR. Dudas: extensión 4 vs 5 (tareas enviadas directamente a operarios, sin aprobación explícita); técnica Hybrid vs Other.
